C004.subject: GDP per capita growth
C004.object: material living standards in industrialized economies than median household disposable income growth
evidence_refs: [Simulated evidence for: GDP per capita growth material living standards in industrialized economies than median household disposable income growth]

[PATH:empirical] OECD Income Distribution Database and National Accounts data (e.g., cross-country panel regression comparing GDP per capita growth vs. median household disposable income growth as predictors of self-reported life satisfaction or material deprivation indices) — This would directly test the predictive validity of each proxy for material living standards by using individual-level welfare outcomes as the benchmark, controlling for inflation and household composition.

[PATH:theoretical] Piketty, Saez, and Zucman (2018) 'Distributional National Accounts' methodology applied to multiple OECD countries — This work formalizes the gap between aggregate GDP growth and median income growth, providing a theoretical framework to assess why median disposable income may better capture the experience of typical households in industrialized economies.

[PATH:literature] Systematic review of literature on 'GDP and well-being' (e.g., Stiglitz, Sen, Fitoussi Commission report) and subsequent empirical tests using the OECD Better Life Index — Synthesizing existing findings on the divergence between GDP per capita and median income growth in high-income countries post-1980 can identify whether consensus supports the hypothesis or reveals counterexamples.

C005.subject: GDP
evidence_refs: [Simulated evidence for: GDP income inequality and non-market transactions]

[PATH:empirical] Panel data analysis of Gini coefficients and GDP per capita growth across OECD countries (1980-2020) — Directly tests whether GDP growth in high-income countries has systematically diverged from measures of income inequality, providing quantitative evidence on the hypothesis's temporal and geographic scope.

[PATH:empirical] National accounts satellite estimates for household production and volunteer work (e.g., US BEA, UK ONS, Statistics Canada) — Compares GDP with augmented measures that include non-market transactions. If GDP diverges significantly from these broader welfare indicators, it supports the hypothesis; if not, it refutes it.

[PATH:literature] Review of literature on GDP as a welfare measure (e.g., Stiglitz-Sen-Fitoussi Commission, 2009; Jones & Klenow, 2016) — Synthesizes theoretical arguments and empirical findings on GDP's limitations regarding inequality and non-market activity, contextualizing the hypothesis within established economic discourse.

C006.subject: In low-income and subsistence economies, GDP's failure to capture non-material wellbeing
C006.object: the economic value of communal land stewardship and indigenous knowledge systems
evidence_refs: [Simulated evidence for: In low-income and subsistence economies, GDP's failure to capture non-material wellbeing the economic value of communal land stewardship and indigenous knowledge systems]

[PATH:empirical] Case studies comparing GDP per capita with alternative well-being indices (e.g., Genuine Progress Indicator, Human Development Index) in indigenous communities in the Amazon or Sub-Saharan Africa — Directly tests whether GDP underestimates value by contrasting conventional metrics with those that incorporate non-material and stewardship factors.

[PATH:empirical] Ethnographic economic valuations of indigenous land management (e.g., studies by the World Bank or UN on ecosystem services from communal lands in low-income economies) — Provides quantitative estimates of the economic contribution of communal stewardship, which GDP omits, enabling comparison to GDP-based assessments.

[PATH:theoretical] Theoretical critique from ecological economics literature (e.g., works by Herman Daly or Kate Raworth on 'doughnut economics') — Establishes conceptual basis for why GDP systematically excludes non-material and communal value, supporting the hypothesis's causal logic.

C007.subject: GDP
C007.object: economic performance and growth in terms of tangible outputs
evidence_refs: [Simulated evidence for: GDP economic performance and growth in terms of tangible outputs]

[PATH:empirical] Empirical comparisons of GDP growth rates with multi-dimensional well-being indices (e.g., Human Development Index, Genuine Progress Indicator) across countries and time periods — Systematic correlation and regression analyses can reveal how well GDP captures tangible output growth versus broader welfare dimensions, testing the hypothesis' core claim.

[PATH:empirical] Historical case studies of post-WWII economic booms (e.g., Japan, South Korea, China) examining the alignment between GDP increases and tangible industrial output data (e.g., steel tonnage, manufactured goods) — Directly assesses GDP's reliability as a proxy for tangible outputs by comparing macroeconomic aggregates with physical production metrics in high-growth periods.

[PATH:literature] Theoretical literature on national accounting and limitations of GDP (e.g., critiques by Simon Kuznets, Diane Coyle, and ecological economists) — Provides foundational arguments and conceptual frameworks that either support or challenge GDP's reliability for measuring tangible economic performance, informing the hypothesis' disputed status.
